children: TVS Motor Company expects India's domestic two-wheeler industry to record high single-digit growth during the festive season, supported by steady customer footfalls and demand across internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric models.
The festive period runs from Onam to Diwali, and includes Krishna Janmashtami, Ganesh Chaturthi, Navratri, Dussehra and Dhanteras.

"As we head into the festive season, we are looking at high single-digit growth," Gaurav Gupta, President, Two-Wheeler India Business, TVS Motor Company, told reporters on the sidelines of the launch of the updated Apache and Ronin motorcycles on September 17.
Gupta said momentum in the two-wheeler industry remained buoyant, although macroeconomic indicators presented a mixed picture. The company witnessed healthy demand during Onam and Ganesh Chaturthi.

Rainfall has been lower than expected. However, reservoir levels remain above the 10-year average, while kharif crop sowing is only marginally lower, according to Gupta. These factors supported the company's optimism, although an element of caution remained.
GST transition distorted last year's base
Gupta observed that last year's festive season did not provide a like-for-like comparison because the Goods and Services Tax (GST) transition altered normal buying patterns.
The government disclosed the revised tax structure on September 3, 2025, while its implementation began on September 22, 2025.

Dealerships remained operational during the intervening period and transactions continued. However, expectations of lower taxes encouraged many customers to postpone purchases, weakening showroom activity and slowing factory-to-dealer supplies.
The sales rose sharply after the new rates took effect as customers who had postponed purchases returned to the market, making last year's base difficult to compare with.
TVS grows faster than industry

The domestic two-wheeler sales of TVS increased 26.63 percent year-on-year to 20,15,314 units during April-August FY27 from 15,91,528 units in the corresponding period last year, according to the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM).

The industry grew 18.74 percent year-on-year to 96,23,709 units during April-August FY27 from 81,05,098 units in the year-ago period. Consequently, the domestic two-wheeler market share of TVS increased to 20.94 percent from 19.64 percent.
The company's two-wheeler exports rose 30.32 percent year-on-year to 7,43,122 units from 5,70,244 units.

Combining domestic wholesales and exports, TVS recorded the highest two-wheeler volumes in June, July and August. Its overall two-wheeler sales stood at 5,91,437 units in August, ahead of Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India at 5,79,210 units and Hero MotoCorp at 5,68,398 units.
EV capacity to increase
TVS plans to increase its monthly electric two-wheeler capacity from the current 40,000-45,000 units to more than 50,000 units over the next three to four months.

The company will look at increasing capacity further during the fourth quarter, depending on demand and the ability of suppliers to raise their output, Gupta said, adding that the Apache motorcycle-manufacturer is also working on alternative technologies to strengthen supply-chain security.

Electric two-wheelers account for around 10 percent of the two-wheeler market so far this year, compared with 6.7 percent last year, according to the company. Penetration remained between 10.5 percent and 11 percent during the past three months.
Gupta noted that TVS was seeing strong customer pull for both the iQube and Orbiter electric scooters, although he did not disclose model-wise volumes.
Premium motorcycle range updated
On September 17, TVS introduced new variants and enhancements across its Apache and Ronin portfolios, with prices ranging from Rs 1,27,990 to Rs 2,87,790 (ex-showroom, New Delhi).

Depending on the model, the updates include traction control, dual-channel ABS, TFT displays with Google Map mirroring, adjustable front suspension, panic brake alert, Type-C charging and keyless operation.
"In many ways, TVS looks at democratising advanced technologies and features for two-wheeler riders in the country," Gupta said.

title: TVS expects domestic two-wheeler market to grow in high single digits this festive season
